title: Review: Tissue fluid and lymph; Haemoglobin and oxygen transport; Ecosystems, populations and niches; Sampling and investigating populations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EC01a#t4 term and clue written for the game; EX06#t4 term and clue written for the game; EX06#t3 term and clue written for the game; EC01a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EC01a#N.3a, EC01b#N.9a, EC02#N.14, EX09#N.7, EC01a#N.11, EC01b#N.2, EC02#N.10, EX09#N.14, EC01a#N.5, EC02#N.11, EX09#N.4, EC02#N.4. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Abiotic factors
items.clue: Non-living influences such as temperature, light, pH and salinity

items.label: Pressure filtration
items.clue: Squeezing of liquid out through the capillary wall at the arteriole end

items.label: Lymph
items.clue: Excess liquid that has drained from around the cells into its own vessels

items.label: Ecosystem
items.clue: All the living things in an area together with their non-living environment

questions.stem: Two groups of great crested newts breed in ponds 5 km apart, and no newt ever moves between the ponds. How should the two groups be described?

options.text: Two populations of one species, because the groups are reproductively isolated from each other.
Two species, because groups that do not interbreed cannot belong to the same species.
One population, because all the newts belong to the same species, wherever they breed.
Two communities, because each pond contains newts together with the other organisms living in it.

questions.stem: A tick attaches to a deer and feeds on its blood for several days before dropping off. Which category of interspecific relationship is this?

options.text: Parasitism, because the tick takes nutrition from a living host without killing it.
Predation, because the tick is an animal feeding on the body of another animal.
Pathogenicity, because the tick is a small organism that harms a much larger one.
Mutualism, because the deer provides the tick with the food that it needs to survive.

questions.explanation: A parasite lives on or in its host, obtains food from it over a period of time and harms it, but does not usually kill it. The tick feeding on the deer's blood fits this exactly.

questions.stem: A student estimates the number of dandelions on a school field. She places ten quadrats in the spots where she can see dandelions growing, counts carefully, and scales up by the area of the field. Which statement about her estimate is correct?

options.text: It will be accurate, because she counted every dandelion in each quadrat carefully.
It will be exact if she places fifty quadrats the same way instead of ten.
It is likely to be too high, because the quadrats were not placed at random.
Choosing spots with dandelions is better than random placement, because it gives typical samples.

questions.explanation: She sampled only where dandelions grow, so her mean density is higher than the field's. Random coordinates give every point an equal chance.

questions.stem: Blood leaves the lungs at pH 7.4, 98% saturated. In a working muscle, pO₂ is 4 kPa and the extra CO₂ has lowered the pH to 7.2. At 4 kPa, saturation is 57% at pH 7.4 and 43% at pH 7.2. By how many percentage points does the saturation of this blood fall in the muscle?
questions.explanation: 98 − 43 = 55 percentage points. The Bohr effect adds 14 points to what low pO₂ alone would release (41).

questions.stem: A fallen, rotting log in a wood holds beetle larvae, woodlice, fungi and bacteria. Inside it are damp, decaying wood and still air. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The log cannot be an ecosystem, because an ecosystem must cover a large area such as a forest.
The log's organisms, with its damp wood and still air, form a small ecosystem.
All the organisms living in the log together form one population.
The fungi and bacteria are not part of the community, because they are neither animals nor plants.

questions.explanation: A community plus its abiotic environment is an ecosystem, whether it is a log, a rock pool or a rainforest.

questions.stem: Koalas (Phascolarctos cinereus) feed on Eucalyptus leaves, are active mainly at night, and are found in eucalypt woodland in eastern Australia where rainfall and temperature stay within particular ranges. Which statement about the ecological niche of the koala is correct?

options.text: Its niche is the eucalypt woodland of eastern Australia in which it lives and feeds
Its niche is fully described by its position as a primary consumer of leaves
Its niche includes its diet and its predators, but not the rainfall and temperature it tolerates
Its niche includes its Eucalyptus diet and its tolerance of rainfall and temperature

questions.stem: In a capture–mark–release–recapture study, 40 woodlice were caught, marked and released. Later, 50 woodlice were caught, of which 10 were marked. What is the Lincoln index estimate of the population? (The Lincoln index is the population estimate from mark–release–recapture data.)

options.text: About 8
About 200
About 2000
About 80

questions.explanation: Population estimate = M × N ÷ R = 40 × 50 ÷ 10 = 200. One fifth of the second sample was marked, so the 40 marked woodlice are estimated to be one fifth of the population.

questions.stem: As blood flows through the lung capillaries, CO₂ diffuses out of it into the alveoli. How does this help the blood load oxygen?

options.text: Haemoglobin's affinity for O₂ rises, so it loads O₂ more fully at the lungs' pO₂.
The curve shifts right, so haemoglobin's affinity rises and it loads more O₂.
Nothing changes, because only the high pO₂ in the lungs affects loading.
CO₂ leaving frees the haem groups it was blocking, so O₂ can bind to them.

questions.explanation: Less CO₂ (and higher pH) shifts the curve left. Higher affinity means fuller loading in the lungs.

questions.stem: A student finds a woodland plant only on the shaded side of a hedge. Which pair names one abiotic factor and one biotic factor that could explain this?

options.text: Light intensity; soil pH
A grazing rabbit; a competing grass
Light intensity; a competing grass
Soil water; air temperature

questions.explanation: Light is non-living (abiotic); a competitor is living (biotic). Either could restrict the plant to the shaded side.

questions.stem: Beetles were marked with a spot of bright paint that made them easier for birds to see. Compared with the true population size, what will the Lincoln index estimate be, and why?

options.text: Too low, because fewer marked beetles are recaptured and fewer recaptures mean a smaller population.
Unaffected, provided the second sample is taken at the release point soon after the beetles are released.
Too low, because fewer beetles in total are encountered across the two samples, so fewer are counted.
Too high, because fewer marked beetles survive to be recaptured, so R is too small.

questions.stem: Adult haemoglobin is about 20% saturated with oxygen at a partial pressure of oxygen of 2 kPa, 60% at 4 kPa, 90% at 8 kPa and 98% at 13 kPa. Which explanation accounts for this pattern?

options.text: The four haem groups fill one after another at equal rates, so saturation rises in direct proportion to the oxygen concentration.
The curve shows the order in which haemoglobin loads over time, from its arrival in the lungs to full saturation.
Saturation rises steeply from 2 to 8 kPa because each oxygen bound raises the affinity of the other haem groups.
The plateau above 8 kPa is where haemoglobin releases most of its oxygen to tissues, because saturation is highest there.

questions.stem: A student places ten 0.5 m × 0.5 m quadrats at random in a 250 m² meadow and counts 20 orchids in total. What is the estimated population of orchids in the meadow?

options.text: 2000 plants
20 plants
500 plants
20000 plants

questions.explanation: Each quadrat is 0.25 m², so the sampled area is 10 × 0.25 = 2.5 m². Density = 20 ÷ 2.5 = 8 orchids per m², and 8 × 250 m² = 2000 orchids.
